claimLimit: These entries are documented programming risks. The cited sources establish technical distinctions, not that a learner held a belief or its prevalence. Author mutants and reviewer counterexamples are controls, not learner-error evidence.

entries.temptingClaim: Correct object fields in a different order describe a different JSON model schema.
entries.correction: Compare object members by name and value. Preserve order for arrays such as vocabulary entries. Byte identity is a separate check.
entries.basis: Citation-backed programming risk; no learner prevalence or recorded learner-error claim. Applying the documented distinction to this original teaching model is author inference.
entries.refutationMarker: Compare object members by name and value. Preserve order for arrays such as vocabulary entries. Byte identity is a separate check.
entries.scopeBoundary: A different serialization still has a different byte digest, which this course deliberately uses as the cache fingerprint.

entries.temptingClaim: A value that JavaScript can convert into a finite number is already a valid numeric score.
entries.correction: Numeric validation must reject strings, null and missing values. The attention mask is the one explicit nonfinite exception.
entries.basis: Citation-backed programming risk; no learner prevalence or recorded learner-error claim. Applying the documented distinction to this original teaching model is author inference.
entries.refutationMarker: Numeric validation must reject strings, null and missing values. The attention mask is the one explicit nonfinite exception.
entries.scopeBoundary: This is the original runtime input policy, not a statement that every JavaScript API must reject coercible values.

entries.temptingClaim: Finite input coordinates guarantee finite intermediate arithmetic.
entries.correction: Squaring or dividing can overflow. Rearrange the same formula to keep intermediate magnitudes bounded.
entries.basis: Citation-backed programming risk; no learner prevalence or recorded learner-error claim. Applying the documented distinction to this original teaching model is author inference.
entries.refutationMarker: Squaring or dividing can overflow. Rearrange the same formula to keep intermediate magnitudes bounded.
entries.scopeBoundary: The examples establish specific binary64 failure modes, not universal guarantees about all numerical algorithms.

entries.temptingClaim: RMSNorm subtracts the row mean just as LayerNorm does.
entries.correction: This RMS normalization rescales by root mean square and learned gains without mean subtraction.
entries.basis: Citation-backed programming risk; no learner prevalence or recorded learner-error claim. Applying the documented distinction to this original teaching model is author inference.
entries.refutationMarker: This RMS normalization rescales by root mean square and learned gains without mean subtraction.
entries.scopeBoundary: PocketDecoder fixes epsilon, dimensions and gains. The source paper does not define this whole architecture.

entries.temptingClaim: A cached next token can restart its position at zero because only one new token is computed.
entries.correction: The new token follows the already processed prefix; its zero-based position equals the old cache length.
entries.basis: Citation-backed programming risk; no learner prevalence or recorded learner-error claim. Applying the documented distinction to this original teaching model is author inference.
entries.refutationMarker: The new token follows the already processed prefix; its zero-based position equals the old cache length.
entries.scopeBoundary: The course uses immutable, fingerprint-bound full-prefix caches and RoPE. It does not implement Transformers cache classes, padding, sliding windows or session-reset APIs.

sources.section: Difference between Number.isFinite() and global isFinite()
sources.support: Number.isFinite requires a Number and does not convert strings or null into numbers. Global isFinite performs conversion, so it is a different validation operation.
